findings.title: Sunset bricks the DAO treasury once the DAO wallet runs the AVM 13 program
findings.scenario: The rollout pushes the AVM 13 wallet to the DAO wallet. Later the sunset deletes the DAO app, then pushes the v11 SunsetContract, and AVM rejects the version downgrade. The wallet admin is now a deleted app, so 47 ALGO, 448,256 AKTA and the manager role of 16 ASAs lock forever.
findings.fix: Compile SunsetContract at avmVersion 13. In both scripts, push SunsetContract into the DAO wallet and simulate the remaining wallet steps before the DAO app is deleted.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed SunsetContract compiles to v11 and the wallet to v13; it did not re-read go-algorand.
findings.conditional: Only if the sunset runs after the DAO wallet moves to the AVM 13 program.
findings.fixNote: Sunset contracts at AVM 13; DAO wallet is retired before the DAO app; simulated first.

findings.title: Sunset staging window lets anyone turn every automatic wallet into SunsetContract
findings.scenario: Step 1 stores SunsetContract as the live factory child, and step 2 swaps the factory in a later execution. Between them, any account calls updateWallet on each automatic wallet, about 16 per group. Each wallet becomes SunsetContract, and funds in its controlled EOA and escrows freeze forever.
findings.fix: Do steps 1 and 2 in one atomic execution group, or let WalletFactorySunsetContract carry the program itself. Add an e2e where a stranger calls updateWallet between the steps.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the two-execution staging gap in execute-deployer-sunset.ts:607-629.
findings.conditional: Only if a sunset script runs. All MainNet wallets are v11 and automatic, so all are exposed then.
findings.fixNote: Child staging and factory swap run in one group.

findings.title: --skip-wallet-child or --split-children leaves the new factory unable to create wallets
findings.scenario: The operator upgrades the wallet factory but skips or splits the wallet child. The factory sends an 11-arg create with a v13 clear program to the v11 child in bc. Every newAccount and updateWallet reverts until someone pushes the child.
findings.fix: Make the wallet child mandatory for the AbstractedAccountFactory target. Or refuse a factory upgrade whose child selector or version does not match the live bc.
findings.verifyNote: Not re-verified by coordinator.
findings.conditional: Only if Phase 2 runs with --skip-wallet-child or --split-children.
findings.fixNote: Wallet child is mandatory with the factory; childPushProblems guard.

findings.title: newAccount with an external controlled address and any plugin always reverts
findings.scenario: A user calls newAccount with an external controlled address C and one plugin. The plugin install sends from C while C is still rekeyed to the factory, so the group reverts. With the order fixed, the user would pay plugin MBR twice.
findings.fix: Install plugins after the rekey to the wallet and do not pre-fund pluginMBR. Or reject plugins when C is external.

findings.title: Recovery clears co-admin keys only until the same domain is set again
findings.scenario: A co-admin passkey K is stolen, and an admin plugin recovers the wallet. The new admin sets the domain back to akita.community, which re-activates every old key, including K. K is a full admin and can take the wallet back.
findings.fix: Bump a domain epoch on recovery and store it with each key. Or document that setDomain after recovery must use a fresh domain.
findings.conditional: Only if an admin or recovery plugin is used; today only mocks/admin-plugin exists.

findings.title: Escrow.delete never succeeds for a wallet escrow, so the sunset escrow step fails
findings.scenario: Each wallet escrow is rekeyed to the wallet app, so its own inner payment fails sender auth. The sunset deleteEscrows step aborts after the DAO is already deleted. Each escrow locks 0.1 ALGO plus 150,000 µA creator MBR, about 6 ALGO for 24 DAO escrows.
findings.fix: Rekey the escrow back to itself through a plugin window before deletion. Or accept the loss and skip the step.
findings.conditional: Matters when the sunset or EscrowFactory.delete runs.

findings.title: coverFees grants allow only one plugin call per window
findings.scenario: _addPlugin now requires cooldown > 0 for coverFees. The plugin cooldown then fails a second plugin call in the same window. Agent and keeper flows that need two calls cannot use fee coverage.
findings.fix: No fix proposed. Document the limit for agent and keeper flows.

findings.title: arc58_canCall with type Admin now reverts for a non-admin reader
findings.scenario: resolveCallerType asserts admin for CallerTypeAdmin. Arbitrary readers simulate the readonly arc58_canCall. It now throws instead of returning false.
findings.fix: No fix proposed. SDK readers must expect the revert.

findings.title: Test-only Arc58AgentRevoker is unauthenticated and its client ships in the SDK
findings.scenario: The contract forwards arc58_removePlugin for anyone. If a deployment sets it as a wallet revocation app, anyone can strip that wallet's plugins. The SDK exports its client and the AgentProbe client like production clients.
findings.fix: Do not export test-only clients from the SDK (same pattern as F8).
findings.conditional: Only if a deployment sets it as a wallet's revocation app.

findings.title: Admin misconfigurations can hand admin power to plugins
findings.scenario: assignDomain(controlledAddress, walletDomain) makes the controlled account a co-admin, so a plugin holding it can call arc58_changeAdmin. arc58_newEscrow with the controlled address makes escrow-scoped allowances stop limiting a plugin.
findings.fix: Reject caller == controlledAddress in assignDomain and address == controlledAddress in newEscrow.
findings.conditional: Needs the admin's own misconfiguration.

findings.title: DAO wallet has caller-specific grants for EOAs that bypass DAO proposals
findings.scenario: Caller YIIMG4OH… holds non-execution-key, unrestricted grants on the DAO wallet main account for NFD 3572944055, ASA manager 3605315701, self-optin 3569560545 and social 3569562087. The factory creator R2MOGX… holds self-optin and ASA-manager grants. These grants act on the treasury with no proposal.
findings.fix: Route to the DAO slice: revoke the grants or record them as accepted operators (see DAO-R3).

findings.title: Update-plugin lease binding is bypassed by any non-execution-key grant
findings.scenario: An AddPlugin proposal (power 300, 5 days) installs the Update plugin for a caller with useExecutionKey = false. That caller sets the rekey txn lease to an old UpgradeApp lease such as dao_upg_78452. The plugin accepts it, so the caller upgrades the DAO, Staking or the wallet factory child to its own code.
findings.fix: In requireUpgradeExecution, require a Global grant, an empty escrow and useExecutionKey for the non-admin branch. Reject expired leases, and class AddPlugin of pal.update as upgrade class.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the plugin trusts the lease of any earlier arc58_rekeyToPlugin txn, and isUpgradeLease has no expiry or used flag.
findings.conditional: Only if a non-execution-key grant of Update-plugin code exists. Today the only grant 3569559689 is global plus execution key.
findings.fixNote: Rekey must use the Update plugin's global, escrow-free, execution-key grant; leases expire; pal.update install is upgrade class.

findings.title: A proposal that misses quorum stays in Voting and can be finalized as Approved later
findings.scenario: A holder submits ChangeAdmin to self and votes Approve. Quorum fails, so finalize reverts and the proposal stays Voting. Months later, locks expire; the holder calls checkpointExpiredLock, finalizes as Approved and executes ChangeAdmin to take the DAO wallet.
findings.fix: When voting has ended and participation is not met, set Rejected instead of asserting. Optionally snapshot the quorum denominator at submit and add an execution deadline.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed finalize uses live locked stake with no deadline, and a quorum miss asserts instead of rejecting.
findings.conditional: Only if live locked stake later drops to X / participation or below, where X is the attacker's locked stake.
findings.fixNote: Locked stake is snapshotted at submit; a quorum miss ends Rejected.

findings.title: initialize() ignores creator or operator grants and pre-upgrade keys
findings.scenario: The DAO wallet already has 11 caller-scoped grants from bootstrap proposals. For example, YIIMG4OH… can use the NFD plugin 3572944055 to sell DAO-owned NFDs such as akita.algo with no vote. All of these grants keep working after initialize().
findings.fix: Refuse bootstrap AddPlugin with caller != zero, or track such grants like keys. Revoke or explicitly accept the 11 grants before initialize.
findings.fixNote: Pre-launch caller-scoped grants are kept on purpose (setup before launch is a feature) and recorded publicly in the DAO (getBootstrapGrants). They do not block initialize(). The revoke script lists them and removes only those named with --revoke, plus weak Update-plugin grants and leftover execution keys.

findings.title: One closed voter account blocks deletion of a proposal forever
findings.scenario: A voter votes and then closes the account. deleteProposalVotes cannot pay 22,500 µALGO to an empty account, so voteCount never reaches 0. deleteProposal reverts forever, and the proposer refund and tally MBR stay locked.
findings.fix: When the voter cannot receive the refund, keep it or pay the treasury. Still delete the box and decrement voteCount.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the unconditional 22,500 µALGO refund and the voteCount === 0 requirement, which locks proposal box MBR.
findings.fixNote: Refund skipped for a closed voter; the box is still deleted.

findings.title: Bootstrap proposals are executable by anyone; MainNet #107 is still Approved
findings.scenario: After the DAO upgrade, anyone calls executeProposal(107). It writes boxes from the DAO's 3.97 ALGO free balance and adds a dead key to the wallet. bootstrapKeyCount rises, so initialize fails until someone calls clearBootstrapKeys.
findings.fix: Require Txn.sender == creator when votingTs == 0. Call deleteProposal(107) right after the upgrade.
findings.conditional: Only after the DAO upgrade while the DAO is still Draft.

findings.title: Validator accepts UpgradeApp actions that can never execute
findings.scenario: A proposal with app = 0, a zero lease, or a used lease passes creation and the vote. executeProposal then reverts. The proposal stays Approved until its proposer cancels it and the full vote runs again.
findings.fix: Check app != 0 and a non-zero lease in the validator. Optionally check lease freshness at creation.

findings.title: Self-freeze settings, large proposal reads, missing guild_fees, old Update plugin power
findings.scenario: Governance can freeze itself with a zero akita_assets id, a wrong aal.staking, or an upgrade power above every lock. getProposal reverts above 1,024 B, and the MainNet DAO has no guild_fees global. An old Update plugin left installed keeps updateFactoryChildContract and updateAkitaDaoAppIDForApp power.
findings.fix: Bound these values in the validator. Keep the Phase 2a removal of the old Update plugin mandatory.

findings.title: Guild treasury wallet is created with automaticUpdates = true
findings.scenario: createWallet passes automaticUpdates = true. Any account can then call factory.updateWallet on the guild treasury and install wallet code the AkitaDAO registered. The guild's own UpdateWallet vote is bypassed, and the guild can never opt out.
findings.fix: Pass false for automaticUpdates in createWallet. Optionally add a governed action that calls setFactoryUpdateSettings.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed contract.algo.ts:836 passes true and factory updateWallet skips the admin check when automatic; rated a product call at Medium.
findings.fixNote: Guild treasuries are created with automaticUpdates = false.

findings.title: Shrinking the electorate re-validates only the 9 class settings
findings.scenario: A 5-member guild sets AddMembers (code 1) to 5 approvals. A RemoveMember passes 3-of-5. No AddMembers proposal can pass now, and changing code 1 settings also needs 5 approvals.
findings.fix: Validate per-code and per-plugin settings in each policy's validateGuildSettings. Re-validate SetPluginSettings at execution.

findings.title: Anyone can squat official consensus program names before the deploy script uploads them
findings.scenario: An observer sees the factory creation and calls initProgram with the name fixed-signers first. The deployer upload reverts, and the name is taken forever in that factory. If a run ignored the error, SDK users could mint guilds with the attacker's consensus program.
findings.fix: Restrict initProgram to the creator or DAO wallet for reserved names. Or have the SDK verify each consensus program hash.

findings.title: An unexecutable Approved proposal can be cleared only by its proposer
findings.scenario: A proposal passes and then becomes unexecutable, for example NewWallet while a wallet exists. Only the proposer can cancel it. An absent proposer locks each voter's 22,500 µALGO receipt and the ballot and snapshot MBR.
findings.fix: Let anyone invalidate an Approved proposal whose actions now fail validation, or one older than N seconds. Refund the reserve as cancelProposal does.

findings.title: Approved proposals always target the current wallet, not a specific one
findings.scenario: After ChangeAdmin and NewWallet, an old Approved wallet action runs against the new treasury. Approved proposals never expire. A treasury migration does not escape a captured-vote proposal.
findings.fix: Settled by Kyle (no expiry). No change.

findings.title: validateOfferings does not mirror the Subscriptions constraints
findings.scenario: Offerings with amount < 3, interval < 60 or a title over MAX_TITLE_LENGTH pass the vote. They then revert at execution. Cancel recovers the reserve.
findings.fix: Mirror the Subscriptions checks in validateOfferings.

findings.title: The DAO revocation app can remove plugins and allowances on guild treasuries
findings.scenario: The wallet's _requireAdminOrRevoke lets the DAO revocation app call arc58_removePlugin, removeNamedPlugin and removeAllowances on guild treasuries. The guild-local plugin box is left orphaned, which is harmless.
findings.fix: Wallet-wide design. No change.

findings.title: No guild actions for arc58_optInEscrow, setBio or setFactoryUpdateSettings
findings.scenario: The guild cannot opt escrows into assets, set a bio, or change factory update settings. This is a feature gap.
findings.fix: Add governed actions if these features are needed.

findings.title: Guild treasury is not in the legacy EscrowFactory registry
findings.scenario: The treasury is created through newAccount with no registry entry. Until the Phase 2 and 3 principal proposals run on MainNet, legacy plugins that resolve origin through the registry treat it as unregistered.
findings.fix: Run the principal-resolution phases before guilds use legacy plugins.

findings.title: Guild plugin trusts any consensus program the factory accepted
findings.scenario: requireGuild checks only factory provenance. A guild minted from the official factory with an attacker-registered consensus name looks official.
findings.fix: Have the SDK allowlist consensus program hashes (part of the GUILD-3 fix).

findings.title: approval = 0 and approval = 100% are configuration hazards
findings.scenario: With approval = 0 and minimumApprovals = N, a proposal passes regardless of rejections. With approval = 100%, any single voter has a veto.
findings.fix: Document these hazards in the SDK.

findings.title: Native swap LP fee rounds down, toward the trader
findings.scenario: With feeBps = 30, a swap with net ≤ 333 pays an LP fee of 0. A trader can split a trade into fee-free slices. The leak is under 1 base unit per swap, so it matters only for high-value, low-decimal assets.
findings.fix: Use mulDivUp(net, pre.feeBps, BpsDivisor) for lpFee.

findings.title: An ASA clawback shortfall bricks every inline sync
findings.scenario: Anyone creates a pool for an ASA with a clawback address. The clawback takes 1 unit from the escrow. Every add, remove and sync then reverts until the admin pauses the pool, and the last emergency exits fail.
findings.fix: Reject pool assets with a non-zero clawback in createPool. Or book a negative surplus as a pro-rata loss.

findings.title: setAdmin is single-step and accepts any account, including zero
findings.scenario: The admin is set to a typo or the zero address. Later a pinned hook or valuator breaks, and swaps on that pool revert. Nobody can pause the pool, so LP funds stay locked forever.
findings.fix: Add a two-step proposeAdmin and acceptAdmin. At least reject the zero address.

findings.title: Receipt units sent to the escrow outside custody are never booked
findings.scenario: Anyone sends 1 receipt unit to the escrow, and the unit is stranded. A later External hook that recalls the whole escrow balance underflows applySigned. The recall reverts until the hook recalls by slot.units.
findings.fix: Make it a hook-author rule to recall by getExternalSlots().units. Or let sync or revalue book surplus receipt units as a donation.
findings.conditional: Only when a production External hook exists; none exists yet.

findings.title: A custody trade can opt the escrow out of a pool asset for good
findings.scenario: On a curve pool, an approved custody hook sends all of asset A out with assetCloseTo and pays enough B. Deposits of A then revert forever, and the pool works one way. No funds are lost.
findings.fix: Optional: after a custody call, assert the escrow is still opted in to both pool assets and every receipt.

findings.title: Hook approval does not require an immutable hook
findings.scenario: The admin approves an updatable third-party hook, and its owner updates it. Every pool pinned to it reverts on its hook points until the admin pauses each pool.
findings.fix: Add 'no UpdateApplication path' to the hook approval checklist, as for valuators.

findings.title: An emergency-exited fungible-curve pool cannot be unpaused safely
findings.scenario: The Vault pro-rata exit leaves the curve aggregate unchanged. The cross-checks then fail on every normal operation. This affects only a future fungible curve, not BinEngine.
findings.fix: Document that such a pool stays paused, or require fungible curves to read req.reserveA/B.

findings.title: Per-stake floor holds; minBinShares can still be set at the 2^32 floor
findings.scenario: The pool creator can set minBinShares at 1 base unit of Y per bin. A ladder of up to 128 dust bins then costs only refundable box MBR. Router slicing still clears it.
findings.fix: Keep the SDK default of one whole Y token.

findings.title: ALGO above MBR in an ASA/ASA pool escrow is not tracked
findings.scenario: Custody measures only the two pool assets and the receipts. A custody hook can spend stray ALGO in an ASA/ASA escrow, for example as inner fees. The amounts are negligible.
findings.fix: No change needed: the escrow is funded at exactly its MBR.

findings.title: LaunchTaxHook books unpaid sell tax; any pool creator can claim other launches' taxes
findings.scenario: An attacker creates a pool with LaunchTax at AfterInitialize|AfterSwap and perms 0, which validateHooks accepts. Each sell accrues tax the Vault never paid, about 450 ALGO per round trip at 500 bps. claim then pays that accrual from the shared hook balance, which holds every launch's unclaimed tax.
findings.fix: Write a pendingSell marker at BeforeSwap and accrue at AfterSwap only when it is set. Also track totalAccrued per asset and assert the hook holding covers it.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed validateHooks does not tie points to perms, the Vault pays outFee only after a pricing point, and the hook accrues unconditionally.
findings.fixNote: Hook books sell tax only after its own BeforeSwap set a per-swap marker; per-asset totals; claims check solvency.

findings.title: LaunchTaxHook F6 underfunding is paid from other owners' accrued ALGO
findings.scenario: An attacker creates pools with LaunchTax, funding = 0 and a fresh quote ASA. Each pool locks about 38,100 µALGO box MBR and 100,000 µALGO opt-in MBR from other owners' accrued tax. Their claims then revert, and on close the attacker gets the box refund it never paid.
findings.fix: At initialize, measure the min-balance growth and assert balance − minBalance ≥ total accrued ALGO. Or require F6 funding to cover the growth; AntiSnipe and GatedFee share the pattern at Low.
findings.fixNote: Initialize asserts the hook still covers all accrued ALGO after its MBR writes.

findings.title: LaunchTax sell tax is stranded when installed without AfterSwap
findings.scenario: A direct creator installs LaunchTax with BeforeSwap but no AfterSwap. The Vault pays the sell tax to the hook, but nothing accrues it and the hook has no sweep. The tax locks forever and grows the balance that DEXEXT-1 and DEXEXT-2 drain.
findings.fix: Add an owner-scoped sweep of holding − totalAccrued per asset. Or refuse such installs in the SDK.

findings.title: LaunchManager accepts a graduation threshold a zero-fee curve can never reach
findings.scenario: A creator sets G = maxRaise with all fees at 0. swapCore keeps rB ≥ 1, so rA never reaches G. The pool bonds forever, M stays locked, and the bounty is never paid.
findings.fix: Require G < maxRaise with a margin, for example G ≤ mulDiv(vA, S − 1, vB + 1).

findings.title: VolatilityFeeHook divides by zero on an empty pool with amountIn = 1
findings.scenario: Quote hooks run before the Vault liquidity check. tryQuoteRoute on an empty pool reverts instead of returning 0. A router swapBest with that candidate then reverts.
findings.fix: Return ctx.feeBps when rA == 0 or rB == 0.

findings.title: Pair-index squatting of LaunchManager tokens
findings.scenario: The token id is public between createToken and launch. Anyone can create pools for it with approved hooks, such as an attacker-owned LaunchTax at 5%. These pools take the first pairPools slots ahead of the official pool.
findings.fix: Frontends and routers take the pool id from LaunchManager.getLaunch, not getPairPools.

findings.title: F6 overfunding is unrecoverable in AntiSnipe and GatedFee
findings.scenario: Neither hook has a withdraw method. A creator who overpays gatedFunding loses the excess. With DEXEXT-2, a creator who underpays draws on that excess.
findings.fix: No fix proposed beyond the DEXEXT-2 funding check.

findings.title: Suspicion: operator toggles can drain the ConsensusKeyreg tank
findings.scenario: If going offline clears IncentiveEligible, each offline and online toggle by the operator costs the tank 2 ALGO. The e2e test only logs eligibility instead of asserting it. The operator is admin-appointed and the loss is bounded by the tank.
findings.fix: Assert eligibility after going offline in consensus-keyreg.e2e.spec.ts.

findings.title: Suspicion: router opt-ins spend outside the guard
findings.scenario: ensureLegOptIn pays 0.1 ALGO per new asset from S before the in0/algo0 snapshot. A caller can spend about 24 × 0.1 ALGO of S per call with junk assets. This matters only if allowances must bound a delegated agent's ALGO spend.
findings.fix: Confirm how the wallet books these opt-ins against allowances.

findings.title: Suspicion: GatedFee passes count only the controlled_address identity
findings.scenario: Passes measure key = controlled_address (decision #18). AKTA locks or impact held by an escrow window's S are not counted.
findings.fix: Design limit. No exploit.

findings.title: ARC-58 tip route makes tippers pay a fresh AKTA opt-in on every tip
findings.scenario: A creator closes the AKTA holding of the origin account after each tip. The next tipper pays 100,000 µA again for the opt-in, which the creator then frees. When the creator posts from an escrow that differs from the wallet origin, tips revert instead.
findings.fix: Decide the route on the account that gets the remainder, and charge the opt-in only when it is not opted in. Or send the remainder through ARC-59 or to the DAO.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator traced the mismatch at the check site only; bounded griefing of 0.1 ALGO per tip.
findings.fixNote: Hinted calls route by the account that receives the remainder. Residual: manual opt-out still re-charges; deployed plugins keep the old route.

findings.title: Legacy terms let anyone drain AkitaSocial free ALGO in repeated cycles
findings.scenario: A user up-votes through a pinned deployed plugin, and AkitaSocial pays the 67,000 µA referral MBR. The user undoes the vote and repeats, at about 3.3 times leverage. MainNet's free 7.64 ALGO is gone after about 115 cycles, and deployed-plugin operations then revert.
findings.fix: Under legacyTerms, pass the zero address as referrer in createVote and createReaction. Otherwise keep K4 monitoring with an alert on free balance.
findings.verifyNote: Per reviewer, an accepted K4 residual; coordinator did not re-verify.
findings.conditional: Only through pinned deployed plugins after the AkitaSocial upgrade.
findings.fixNote: Legacy up-votes and reacts pay no referral.

findings.title: Referral disbursement MBR and unclaimed referral AKTA stay in Rewards for good
findings.scenario: AkitaSocial creates a Rewards disbursement for each referred fee. Only the creator can withdraw credits, reclaim or close, and AkitaSocial has no method for that. The ALGO and unclaimed AKTA lock and grow with usage.
findings.fix: Add a permissionless AkitaSocial.closeReferralDisbursement(id) and reclaimExpired that send proceeds to the DAO escrow or app float.

findings.title: RefTypeAddress accepts any 32-byte key that does not exist yet
findings.scenario: An attacker votes with RefTypeAddress on a pending post key, so the victim's post fails errPostExists. The attacker can also pre-squat padded asset or app keys. Tips on those pages then go to the DAO, not the real creator.
findings.fix: For RefTypeAddress, require a real account, for example an existing meta or a non-zero minBalance.

findings.title: Legacy dual-read trusts every pre-cutoff post; S-01 stays open until the upgrade
findings.scenario: Before the upgrade, anyone creates a lookalike post and a legacy vote on it. The cutoff stamps lazily, so both posts count as pre-cutoff. After the upgrade, editVote on the real post consumes the staged entry.
findings.fix: Re-run the prefix-collision and orphan scans right before and right after the proposal executes. Decide tallies per D4b if a collision appears.

findings.title: Reactions through deployed plugins overpay 3,200 µA each with no refund
findings.scenario: Under legacyTerms the reactor pays 18,900 µA, but the y box costs 15,700 µA. deleteReaction refunds 15,700 µA. Each reaction through an old plugin loses 3,200 µA to AkitaSocial.
findings.fix: Accept and document it. Or mark legacy-paid records and refund 18,900 µA.

findings.title: Ban and block can be bypassed through another escrow of the same wallet
findings.scenario: isBanned and isBlocked key on the spender. A banned or blocked user can act from another escrow of the same wallet.
findings.fix: Also check p.principal in hinted entry points.

findings.title: Plugin reply and react break on non-32-byte or custom refs
findings.scenario: ref.toFixed({ length: 32 }) asserts the length, so asset and app refs revert. For custom types the plugin passes the raw ref, not sha256(type‖ref). The reaction quote is then wrong and the call reverts.
findings.fix: No fix proposed. Handle 8-byte and custom refs in the plugin.

findings.title: Quote and target disagree on same-wallet creators
findings.scenario: The plugin evaluates tipWallet while S is rekeyed to the plugin, and the target evaluates it after rekeyBack. For a creator that is another account of the acting wallet, the call reverts errIpay. Only the creator's own actions are affected.
findings.fix: No fix proposed.

findings.title: Error strings and paywall pricing change on all four live apps
findings.scenario: Errors change from ERR:XXXX to errXxxx. createPayWall now needs exactly 9,300 + 6,800·N with no legacy shim. Old SDK error decoding and paywall quotes break.
findings.fix: Ship the SDK in lockstep with the upgrade.

findings.title: Legacy shims are open to every caller
findings.scenario: Only the payment terms are pinned. Registry referrer, raw meta.wallet tip routing and gate subject Txn.sender stay available to any caller of an old selector. This matches deployed semantics.
findings.fix: No change. SOCIAL-1 still applies to admin-updated wallets.

findings.title: Creator impact is now computed without spot holdings
findings.scenario: The tip tax uses getUserImpactWithInputs without spot holdings (S-06). Creators who hold AKTA or NFTs pay more tax than before.
findings.fix: Communicate the economic change.

findings.title: Subscription gate stays active a full unpaid window; paying every other window suffices
findings.scenario: A subscriber pays at the start of window 2 and keeps escrow below the amount. Keepers cannot trigger window 3, but the gate stays true. The subscriber pays again in window 4 right before use, so the merchant gets 50% for continuous access.
findings.fix: Make active mean lastPayment ≥ currentWindowStart, or allow a small fixed grace such as 1 day. Apply the same rule in social/impact.algo.ts isSubscribed.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed one payment covers its own window plus the next; grace versus revenue leak is a product call.
findings.fixNote: One paid-up rule: current window, or previous window within min(1 day, interval/4). Also fixes SUBGATE-4.

findings.title: SubscriptionsPlugin trusts getSpendingAccount of an unverified wallet
findings.scenario: An attacker deploys app X with spending_address set to the plugin address. Each optIn(X, …) call sends at least 100,000 µALGO from the plugin to Subscriptions. The plugin spare balance drains, and plugin newService with a longer description reverts.
findings.fix: Use getControlledSpendingAccount(wallet) in every SubscriptionsPlugin method.
findings.conditional: The old live plugin 3569561107 is immutable and holds 1,563,300 µALGO (min 256,500).

findings.title: Self-trigger through the new plugin with rekeyBack = true fails for legacy gated subscriptions
findings.scenario: A gated subscription made through a legacy shim stores no principal pair. The plugin computes the gate ctx while the key address is rekeyed to it, but the target computes it after the rekey back. The ctx differs and the call fails errFgte.
findings.fix: Send the trigger with rekeyBack = false and rekey back in a trailing payment. Or ignore at-rest ownership in triggerCtx case 3 when key.address == Txn.sender.

findings.title: Subscribe-time payment does not count at the start of window 2
findings.scenario: lastPayment equals startDate. From startDate + interval until a keeper triggers, the gate returns false for a new subscriber with full escrow. A GatedFee pass measured in that gap loses its gate bit for passTtl.
findings.fix: Use one boundary rule in the gate and the streak, together with the SUBGATE-1 fix.
findings.fixNote: Fixed with SUBGATE-1.

findings.title: ASA subscribe reverts for referred wallets when both fee percentages are 0
findings.scenario: The quote always adds the referral MBR when a referrer exists. createSubscription spends it only when akitaFees > 0, and the ASA path asserts an exact payment. Plugin ASA subscribes from referred wallets then fail.
findings.fix: Return 0 from referralFeeTo when the fee base is 0. Or accept ≥ and escrow the surplus, as the ALGO path does.
findings.conditional: Only if the DAO sets paymentPercentage and triggerPercentage to 0.

findings.title: Gate v2 allowlist governance and fallback behavior
findings.scenario: Until sealImports, the deployer EOA alone controls the allowlist. Removing a sub-gate from the allowlist does not stop existing gates from calling it. Subscription and referrer sub-gates allowlisted without ctxAware fall back to the registry rule, so new wallets fail them.
findings.fix: Use allowlist-sub-gates.ts, which sets ctx flags from the artifact; deploy-universe.ts and deploy-gates.ts do not allowlist.

findings.title: Pass repricing cut-over can under-refund a same-second legacy subscription
findings.scenario: passesCharged uses startDate < passesRepricedAt. A legacy subscription created in the upgrade block gets 83,700 instead of 418,900 back. No MainNet service has passes.
findings.fix: Set passesRepricedAt = latestTimestamp + 1.

findings.title: Minor notes: self-referral rebate, Merkle gate tree type, blocked subscriber access
findings.scenario: Any user can set themselves as referrer and take referrerPercentage of their own Akita fees, as before. MerkleAddressGate accepts any tree type and needs a proof of at least 2 elements. getActiveSubscription ignores merchant blocks until the grace ends.
findings.fix: No contract change proposed.

findings.title: A second reward's preparation disqualifies entries mid-round and shifts Shuffle ranges
findings.scenario: Shuffle reward A is in Allocation, and its winning tickets are computable from the beacon. In one group the attacker starts reward B, moves stake out of chosen entries and lets B's preparation disqualify them. Ranges shift so A's tickets land on the attacker's entries, or the round stalls with errShuffleExhausted.
findings.fix: Allow one open round per pool with assertNoOpenRound in startDisbursement. Or snapshot per-round eligibility.
findings.verifyNote: Not re-verified by coordinator.
findings.fixNote: One open reward round per pool.

findings.title: One balance backs many HARD or SOFT entries across preparation batches
findings.scenario: An attacker has capital C and k sybil entries. They run preparation one entry at a time and move the same stake between sybils between batches. Each sybil counts with weight C, so the attacker takes k times a fair share from honest stakers.
findings.fix: For HARD, require info.lastUpdate < round start. For SOFT, forbid Percentage and Shuffle, or require LOCK or HEARTBEAT for value-weighted rewards.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed per-batch checks at a caller-chosen time and free HARD withdraw; exact payout impact is per reviewer.
findings.fixNote: HARD stakes must predate the round start; SOFT pools reject Percentage and Shuffle. Residual: SOFT Flat/Even.

findings.title: Disbursement box MBR constant undercharges 3,200 µA per disbursement
findings.scenario: MinDisbursementsMBR is 41,700 µA, but the real box costs 44,900 µA. With Rewards v2 funded at only 100,000 µA, the next ASA referral payout fails its min balance and reverts the auction, listing or raffle operation. Later each open disbursement eats 3,200 µA of pooled ALGO.
findings.fix: Drop usedMbrCredits from the v2 struct so 41,700 is exact again. Do not raise the constant, because live immutable children pay exactly 41,700.
findings.verifyNote: Not re-verified by coordinator.
findings.conditional: The revert case needs Rewards v2 funded with only 100,000 µA; v1 already lost 146 × 3,200 µA of its buffer.
findings.fixNote: usedMbrCredits dropped, so 41,700 is exact; SDK reads both box layouts.

findings.title: Rewards plugin cannot withdraw credits or close disbursements
findings.scenario: The plugin has no withdrawMbrCredits or closeDisbursement and always resolves the registry Rewards app. A wallet creator's MBR credits are stranded. The DAO already has 21.33 ALGO of credits stranded on v1 and exposed to the C-1 drain.
findings.fix: Add withdrawMbrCredits and closeDisbursement with an explicit rewardsApp, validated against the current and legacy Rewards IDs or DAO-pinned.
findings.verifyNote: Not re-verified by coordinator.
findings.fixNote: Rewards plugin gains withdrawMbrCredits/closeDisbursement (current or create-pinned legacy app); v1 withdraw script.

findings.title: Legacy flat-charged entries get 1,200 µA more refund than their boxes free
findings.scenario: Legacy plugins pay a flat 50,600 µA, but the freed boxes are worth 49,400 µA. The creator assigns all free ALGO to budgets, then entrants exit. Each exit takes 1,200 µA of reserved ALGO, so preparation or the last withdrawReward later fails.
findings.fix: Exclude the surplus from freeFunds. Or call assertAlgoReservesCovered() at the end of removeEntry.

findings.title: abortRound mode 0 on a current-Rewards disbursement locks allocated rewards
findings.scenario: The creator or DAO aborts with mode 0 after some batches were allocated. The disbursement stays unfinalized, so nobody can claim, reclaim or close it. Those funds were already taken from the budget.
findings.fix: Reject mode 0 when the active disbursement has allocations. Better, store the Rewards app ID with the round.

findings.title: Pools never opt Rewards into the reward ASA, so a fresh v2 stalls ASA rounds
findings.scenario: After the switch to v2, the first ASA round pays the royalty and creates the disbursement. It then reverts at allocation because Rewards is not opted in. Anyone can fix it by paying Rewards.optIn (0.1 ALGO).
findings.fix: Opt Rewards in from the pool optIn, or before createAsaUserAllocations.

findings.title: total += weight in preparation can overflow and block every reward
findings.scenario: A typed pool lists a high-supply asset with at least 2^60 base units held. With STAKE-2 cycling, k sybils × C overflow uint64. Every preparation batch reverts until the sybils leave.
findings.fix: Saturate or assert per entry, or cap quantity.

findings.title: Suspicion: VRF retry can be spammed to push the raffle round forward
findings.scenario: raffle increments vrfFailureCount on every empty beacon reply, and each increment moves the target round by 4. Many raffle calls before the beacon publishes push the target far ahead. This liveness grief is pre-existing since HEAD.
findings.fix: Confirm the real beacon's get semantics and retention window.

findings.title: Suspicion: roundRewards is keyed only by disbursementID
findings.scenario: A future Rewards v3 switch with live pools would mix v2 and v3 IDs. This is moot today because no pools exist.
findings.fix: Store the Rewards app ID with the round before any v3 switch.

findings.title: Anyone can delete the AuctionPlugin v3 app
findings.scenario: PuyaTs routes a method named deleteApplication as the DeleteApplication handler, with no auth. An attacker ends a cheap own auction, points a fake app's spending_address at an EOA rekeyed to the plugin, and calls with OnCompletion DeleteApplication. The factory delete succeeds, so the AVM deletes the shared plugin for every wallet.
findings.fix: Rename the TS method and use @abimethod({ name: 'deleteApplication', allowActions: 'NoOp' }) to keep selector 0xbedfc93b. Have getControlledSpendingAccount require isAkitaWallet.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the DeleteApplication routing and the forward to deleteAuctionApp; the fake-wallet path was not traced end to end.
findings.fixNote: deleteApplication is NoOp-only; selector kept.

findings.title: Auction and Raffle ASA prizes are not protected against clawback or freeze
findings.scenario: A seller who holds clawback on the prize ASA starts a raffle or auction. After entries or bids, the seller claws the prize back. The winner gets 0 units while the seller gets full proceeds; with freeze, claims and refunds lock forever.
findings.fix: Reject prize ASAs with clawback, and preferably freeze, in both factories. Or store prizeAmount and switch to a refund path when the balance changes.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the factory checks sender, receiver, amount and bid asset only, with no clawback or freeze check.
findings.fixNote: Prize ASAs with clawback or freeze are rejected.

findings.title: VRF reveal can stall forever because its timing does not match the MainNet beacon
findings.scenario: The beacon answers round r from ceil8(r) and publishes 2 rounds late. If raffleRound ≡ 1 mod 8, a reveal at raffleRound + 8 reads empty and re-commits with the same residue. A griefer repeats this at about 1 txn per 16 rounds and locks prizes, proceeds and weights MBR.
findings.fix: Commit to a multiple of 8, reveal at least 4 rounds after it, and do not re-commit on an empty read before MAX_WAIT. Update the SDK drawReadyRound to match.
findings.fixNote: Commit to a multiple of 8, reveal 4 rounds later, no re-commit on empty read before 1,000 rounds.

findings.title: Zero-fee auctions charge weights MBR that is never refunded
findings.scenario: A seller or UI creates an auction with bidFee = 0 and weightsListCount = 3. The seller pays 39.34 ALGO extra, which stays in the factory. The measured refund on delete or cancel never returns it.
findings.fix: Assert bidFee > 0 or weightsListCount === 0 in validateRaffleConfig. Or charge weights only when bidFee > 0, also in newAuctionCost.
findings.fixNote: Zero-fee auctions need weightsListCount 0.

findings.title: One opted-out ASA receiver blocks sequential refunds and settlement
findings.scenario: A griefer enters a raffle with ASA tickets and then closes out the ticket ASA. When the raffle fails, refundMBR reverts at the griefer's index forever. Later entrants' tickets, entry MBR and the seller's 52.45 ALGO weights MBR lock until the griefer opts back in.
findings.fix: Use sendBidAssetOrDisburse and sendTicketsOrDisburse in these paths. Or let refundMBR skip a receiver that is not opted in and record a claimable credit.
findings.fixNote: Opted-out receivers are paid through a Rewards claim.

findings.title: A 1-unit donation makes an ASA listing unsellable
findings.scenario: A listing sells 1,000 units of a token. Anyone sends 1 unit to the listing address. Every purchase then reverts with errPchg until the seller delists and relists.
findings.fix: Use >= instead of === for the prize balance check.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the strict === on prize balance; close-out already sweeps, so >= is safe.
findings.fixNote: Listing accepts a prize balance at or above the stored amount.

findings.title: Prize-box transfer sender is not bound in the Auction and Raffle factories
findings.scenario: The factories do not assert prizeBoxTransferTxn.sender === Txn.sender. Anyone can auction or raffle a prize box left owned by a factory and become its seller.
findings.fix: Mirror marketplace.algo.ts:403.

findings.title: Auction factory does not use assertSafeAssetTransfer on the prize transfer
findings.scenario: assetCloseTo, clawback-sourced transfers and rekeys are not rejected. Any excess lands in the factory, which is the seller's own loss.
findings.fix: Use assertSafeAssetTransfer, as Raffle and Marketplace do.

findings.title: ALGO settlement under 0.1 ALGO to an empty account reverts
findings.scenario: Settlement and refund payments under 0.1 ALGO to a closed account revert. This covers Listing and Auction completeAlgoPayments. Anyone can unblock it by funding the account.
findings.fix: Liveness only. Fund the account to unblock.

findings.title: A beacon value that ages out can be re-rolled
findings.scenario: If nobody reveals within about 70 minutes of the value appearing (about 1,512 rounds), a disfavored party can re-roll it. The TRADE-3 MAX_WAIT keeps this but narrows it.
findings.fix: Keep MAX_WAIT inside the beacon window.

findings.title: K8 float DoS on Marketplace listings
findings.scenario: Legacy-paid ALGO listings lock 164,000 µA of factory free balance each. About 8 listings exhaust the margin above the 500,000 µA reserve. Deployed-plugin users then cannot list until someone tops up the factory.
findings.fix: Accepted risk (K8). Monitor and top up.

findings.title: Escrow repoint after factory opt-in adds unbudgeted opt-in MBR
findings.scenario: If the DAO repoints akitaDAOEscrow after the factory opted into an ASA, sendToAkitaEscrow in a child pays (1 + splits) × 0.1 ALGO of unbudgeted opt-in MBR. The claim reverts until someone donates ALGO.
findings.fix: No fix proposed. Plan escrow repoints with this cost in mind.

findings.title: PrizeBox accepts freeze-enabled assets
findings.scenario: optin checks clawback only. A seller who holds the freeze address can freeze the contents after the sale.
findings.fix: Also reject assets with freeze != zero.

findings.title: Listing getAmounts has no tiny-amount fallback
findings.scenario: With a high creator royalty and a price near 4, every purchase underflows. This affects only the seller's own listing, which they can reprice.
findings.fix: Add the tiny-amount fallback that Auction and Raffle use.

findings.title: PrizeBoxFactory 3569557972 has 0 balance, so the first mint reverts
findings.scenario: mint sends Global.minBalance from the payment to the box. The factory's own 0.1 ALGO base and the new app MBR are then uncovered. The first mint reverts until someone funds the factory.
findings.fix: Fund the factory with at least 0.1 ALGO.

findings.title: Deployed AuctionPlugin 3569561141 quotes bid MBR from stale constants
findings.scenario: On new children, its ASA bids always fail the payment.amount === mbr check. ALGO bids land 400 to 800 µA lower than requested.
findings.fix: Move wallets to the new AuctionPlugin after TRADE-1 is fixed.
findings.conditional: Only after new Auction children exist.

findings.title: NFD purchase pays the seller's current price with no buyer bound
findings.scenario: A user or delegated caller submits purchase, expecting the listed 100 ALGO. The NFD owner lands offerForSale at 10,000 ALGO first. The plugin reads the new price and pays it from the wallet's spending account.
findings.fix: Add maxPrice: uint64 and assert the sale amount ≤ maxPrice. The NFD v2 redeploy makes the ABI change free.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed purchase pays btoi(sellamt) read at execution with no caller bound.
findings.fixNote: purchase, renew and autoRenew take maxPrice. Residual: caller picks the cap on Global/agent grants.

findings.title: Haystack plugin can reimburse one router input several times in one group
findings.scenario: A caller with a swap grant puts two swap calls in one rekey window and one relay payment to the router. Both calls match the same input, so the wallet pays the relay twice. The attacker nets A per extra call, up to about 13 calls per group.
findings.fix: Make reimbursement single-use, for example store groupId plus the funding index and reject reuse. Add a regression test with two swap calls.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed findFundingTxnIndex has no used marker; the exploiter needs a swap grant and the loss is bounded by the allowance.
findings.conditional: Only for a caller that holds a swap grant, such as a delegated agent, keeper or Global caller.
findings.fixNote: Funding search stops at the next call to the plugin, so each input pays once.

findings.title: Revenue Manager Flat split stalls allocation when a balance is below the flat value
findings.scenario: The DAO sets [Flat 5 ALGO, Remainder]. Any managed ASA with fewer than 5,000,000 base units reverts the cycle. The cycle stays stuck until a DAO skipEscrowAllocation proposal runs.
findings.fix: Use min(value, remaining) for Flat and compute percentages on the post-flat base. Or reject Flat in validateSplits.
findings.conditional: Only with a DAO Flat split configuration.

findings.title: optIn still creates RM-funded managedAssets boxes that are never deleted
findings.scenario: A user drives a factory child to opt the DAO escrow into a junk ASA. RM pays a box of about 14.5 mALGO with no delete path. Each such asset adds one item to every daily cycle.
findings.fix: Require payment to RM for the box, restrict registrable assets, or add a DAO unmanageAsset.

findings.title: HyperSwap MBR deposits are not bound to the caller; a closed payor blocks release
findings.scenario: Party A pays its leaf MBR from a throwaway account T and then closes T. Every release of A's leaf refunds 34,900 µALGO to T and fails. Anyone can unblock it by funding T with 0.1 ALGO.
findings.fix: Use assertSafePayment(mbrPayment, Txn.sender) on accept and escrowAsa.

findings.title: Live PollPlugin new breaks after the PollFactory upgrade
findings.scenario: newPollCost now includes 200,000 µALGO of page MBR. The live PollPlugin hard-codes 100,000 µALGO, and new asserts an exact payment. Every wallet poll creation through the old plugin reverts until users reinstall the new plugin.
findings.fix: Ship the PollPlugin redeploy and the DAO grant swap in the same proposal set as the factory update. Add the old plugin to the SDK legacy list.
findings.verifyNote: Coordinator confirmed the factory side: newPollCost includes programPagesMbr and createPoll asserts an exact payment.
findings.conditional: Only after the PollFactory upgrade.
findings.fixNote: New PollPlugin grant swaps before the PollFactory upgrade.

findings.title: HyperSwap freeze/clawback assets, Welcome automatic updates, OptIn id stability
findings.scenario: A party that controls freeze or clawback on its own escrowed ASA can block its leaf after the others release. Welcome always creates wallets with automaticUpdates = true, which matters for the sunset window. A new OptIn id would break every wallet's Global grant.
findings.fix: Clients warn on leaf assets with freeze or clawback. Do not redeploy OptIn, SelfOptIn or AsaManager.

findings.title: Suspicion: NFD autoRenew may pay an inflated segment price
findings.scenario: autoRenew pays whatever getRenewPrice returns, with no cap. If segment renewals use the root owner's i.segmentPriceUsd, the root owner could raise it and trigger autoRenew through a Global grant.
findings.fix: Add an owner-configured maxRenewPrice.

findings.title: Suspicion: Haystack relay may recover its input after reimbursement
findings.scenario: The plugin binds only router calls whose selector equals routerMethod. If the router has another entry that returns unused input to the sender, the relay could get its input back.
findings.fix: Confirm from the production router TEAL.

findings.title: New StakingPool child needs Staking and Rewards methods the live apps lack
findings.scenario: Phase 2 stages the new child, and a creator makes a SOFT pool. Every removeEntry reverts on releaseAppStake, which live Staking does not route. Entry MBR stays locked, and zero-paid rounds revert on closeDisbursement while aal.rewards is v1.
findings.fix: Make the StakingPoolFactory target refuse unless aal.staking and aal.rewards route every selector the child embeds. Order the Staking upgrade and Rewards v2 repoint before the push.
findings.conditional: Only if the StakingPool child is pushed before the Staking upgrade and the Rewards v2 repoint.
findings.fixNote: StakingPoolFactory target refused until Staking and Rewards route every selector the child calls.

findings.title: HyperSwap upgrade removes accept, which installed plugins still call
findings.scenario: After update-hyper-swap.ts runs, wallets with the old HyperSwapPlugin (installed in 7 wallets) can still create offers. Every accept through that plugin reverts. No funds are lost, but the plugin is broken until users reinstall.
findings.fix: Record the removal as a decision, ship the new HyperSwapPlugin and getPluginUpdate with the upgrade, and route it through the Phase 2 ABI guard.
findings.fixNote: accept removal recorded as a decision; HyperSwap goes through the ABI guard and ships its new plugin.

findings.title: Generic update scripts bypass Phase 2 guards; update:wallet-factory breaks creation
findings.scenario: An operator runs update:wallet-factory without --update-factory, as update-dao-wallet.ts suggests. The old factory now pairs the v13 wallet with its v11 clear program. Every newAccount and updateWallet on MainNet fails until someone re-stages the old child.
findings.fix: Make runUpdate refuse Phase 2 targets and child AVM mismatches. Make update-wallet-factory.ts refuse child-only on an old factory, and fix the update-dao-wallet.ts text.
findings.conditional: Only if an operator runs a generic update script instead of the Phase 2 path.
findings.fixNote: runUpdate refuses Phase 2 targets and mismatched children.

findings.title: Resuming a Phase 2 proposal after the DAO upgrade rebuilds the wrong binding
findings.scenario: A target's UpgradeApp executes on the deployed DAO, but its groups are not sent. Then --target AkitaDAO runs. On resume the script picks lease mode, the rebuilt group does not match, and the proposal must be re-proposed.
findings.fix: On resume, use the binding the proposal was built with. Try proposal mode first when executions(lease) exists and no u entry does.
findings.conditional: Only if a Phase 2 proposal is left unsent across the DAO upgrade.

findings.title: Wallet AVM 13 rollout has no canary; the spec order for the DAO wallet cannot run
findings.scenario: Once the wallet child executes, anyone can push AVM 13 code into all 74 automatic wallets, and AVM forbids a downgrade. Spec §9.5 step 4 cannot run before Phase 2. Until the DAO wallet updates, RemoveNamedPlugin reverts.
findings.fix: Decide on a canary explicitly, correct the runbook order, and add a wallet selector check to --unname-aliases. Note that ACCT-3 shows --skip-wallet-child breaks wallet creation.

findings.title: update-meta.ts targets the immutable MetaMerkles app
findings.scenario: Running it creates an UpgradeApp proposal whose group always reverts. If metaMerkles is later repointed to Meta, live consumers lose every root stored in the old app.
findings.fix: Point update-meta.ts at the Meta receipt id. Add the Meta data-migration decision to the runbook before any repoint.

findings.title: Ordering is not encoded for several new apps and plugins outside Phase 3
findings.scenario: StakingPlugin, HyperSwapPlugin, AkitaDAOPlugin, GuildPlugin and Guild call selectors their live targets lack. Phase 2 children call Gate.mustCheckFor, which Gate v1 lacks. Deploying these first gives grants that revert, with no fund loss.
findings.fix: Extend the phase3Gaps readiness check to every deploy script and to Phase 2 children (aal.gate, aal.staking, aal.rewards).

findings.title: Keep the deployed DAO in Draft until --target AkitaDAO has run
findings.scenario: The deployed DAO still has DAO-01, DAO-02 and DAO-03. If it is initialized first, a weak ExecutePlugin proposal can append groups to an approved UpgradeApp lease. planSponsorship also omits the DAO's own 3,492,500 µA.
findings.fix: Do not call initialize before the DAO upgrade. fundTarget covers the DAO sponsorship later.
findings.conditional: Only if the DAO is initialized before its upgrade.

findings.title: Suspicion: rehearsal never runs Phase 2a/2 against the deployed DAO wallet program
findings.scenario: The universe's DAO wallet runs the tree wallet, not f59520de0e45. Selectors match, but group validation on the AVM 11 program is untested.
findings.fix: Rehearse Phase 2a and 2 with the deployed DAO wallet program.

findings.title: Suspicion: static StakingPool creation quotes go stale
findings.scenario: The new 12,660 B child costs 3 more pages (300,000 µA) and about 447 µA fee surcharge per creation. Third-party SDKs or frontends that quote statically will be short.
findings.fix: Update published SDKs and frontends.

rolloutOrder.step: Fix the blockers in new immutable apps before their first deploy
rolloutOrder.why: Hooks, Vault, sub-gates, consensus programs and plugins cannot be patched after deploy.
rolloutOrder.source: DEXEXT-1, TRADE-1, MISC-1, GUILD-3, SUBGATE-1, DEXCORE-2, DAO-R1

rolloutOrder.step: Keep the DAO in Draft until the DAO upgrade has run
rolloutOrder.why: The deployed DAO still has DAO-01, DAO-02 and DAO-03, and initialize opens them to weak proposals.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy RewardsPlugin v2 with withdrawMbrCredits and closeDisbursement
rolloutOrder.why: No current path lets the DAO pull its credits from Rewards v1.

rolloutOrder.step: Withdraw the DAO's 21.33 ALGO mbrCredits from Rewards v1
rolloutOrder.why: The C-1 drain is live on immutable v1; this step needs RewardsPlugin v2 and cuts the ALGO at risk to the ~9.4 ALGO buffer.

rolloutOrder.step: Ask the 13 recipient EOAs to claim from Rewards v1 directly
rolloutOrder.why: No plugin path reaches v1 after the registry switch, and unclaimed value stays drainable.

rolloutOrder.step: Top up the DAO app and fund the DAO wallet for size sponsorship
rolloutOrder.why: The DAO app has 3.97 ALGO free for about 20 bootstrap UpgradeApps, and page growth needs 10,448,500 µA on the DAO wallet.

rolloutOrder.step: Re-run the social prefix-collision and orphan scans
rolloutOrder.why: Lookalikes staged before the upgrade stay consumable after it.

rolloutOrder.step: Run Phase 2a: deploy Update plugin U2, grant it, and remove 3569559689
rolloutOrder.why: The deployed Update plugin cannot push programs over 8 KB or grow pages, and an old Update plugin keeps upgrade power.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade AkitaDAO from 3 to 4 extra pages through a bootstrap UpgradeApp
rolloutOrder.why: It needs Phase 2a; doing it before other Phase 2 proposals avoids the resume binding mismatch.

rolloutOrder.step: Delete proposal #107
rolloutOrder.why: Anyone can execute it after the DAO upgrade and block initialize.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy the new DAOProposalValidator and repoint oal while in Draft
rolloutOrder.why: The live validator rejects Reclaim, ChangeAdmin, the new *_ps keys and the guild_fees field.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade AbstractedAccountFactory with its wallet child in one group
rolloutOrder.why: Needs Phase 2a; skipping the child or using update-wallet-factory.ts child-only stops all wallet creation, and AVM 13 is irreversible.

rolloutOrder.step: Push the new wallet program to the DAO wallet
rolloutOrder.why: RemoveNamedPlugin needs arc58_getNamedPluginKey, which the live wallet program does not route.

rolloutOrder.step: Run RemoveNamedPlugin and --unname-aliases
rolloutOrder.why: These revert until the DAO wallet runs the new wallet program.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade Staking, then set the heartbeat manager through a new StakingPlugin
rolloutOrder.why: The StakingPool child and locked-token guilds need releaseAppStake and G-5, and HEARTBEAT entries fail until beats start.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy Rewards v2 with STAKE-3 fixed or buffered, opt it into ASAs, and repoint aal.rewards
rolloutOrder.why: It must follow the v1 credit withdrawal and precede the StakingPool child, which calls closeDisbursement.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade StakingPoolFactory with its child
rolloutOrder.why: The child calls Staking and Rewards methods that exist only after the two steps before.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy Gate v2 and 16 sub-gates, run allowlist-sub-gates.ts, sealImports, and repoint aal.gate
rolloutOrder.why: Hinted gated paths in Subscriptions and Phase 2 children call Gate.mustCheckFor, which Gate v1 lacks.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade Subscriptions to 4 extra pages
rolloutOrder.why: It needs Phase 2a and the DAO wallet sponsorship, and its hinted gated paths need Gate v2.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy and fund the new SubscriptionsPlugin
rolloutOrder.why: It calls hinted selectors that only the upgraded Subscriptions routes, and newService needs at least 0.1 ALGO + 1,263,300 µALGO in the plugin.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade SocialImpact and SocialModeration
rolloutOrder.why: They are ABI-compatible and come before Graph and AkitaSocial in the social order.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade Graph and AkitaSocial together, then re-run the scans
rolloutOrder.why: AkitaSocial needs 5 extra pages through Phase 2a and a 3,528,000 µA sponsorship.

rolloutOrder.step: Ship the SDK with SOCIAL_HINTED_TARGETS, then deploy the Phase 3 social plugin
rolloutOrder.why: Error codes and paywall pricing change, and the new plugin needs the hinted targets live.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy Meta as a new app, seed types 0 to 6 in order, and repoint metaMerkles
rolloutOrder.why: Every HyperSwap offer reverts with errNoTreeType until the types exist, and MetaMerkles cannot be upgraded.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade HyperSwap with the new HyperSwapPlugin in the same set
rolloutOrder.why: The upgrade removes the accept selector that the old plugin calls.

rolloutOrder.step: Upgrade PollFactory with PollPlugin v2 and the grant swap in one proposal set
rolloutOrder.why: The old plugin's new reverts on the new page MBR quote.

rolloutOrder.step: Fund AuctionFactory, then upgrade the Auction, Raffle and Marketplace factories
rolloutOrder.why: bc growth takes 341,200 µA from AuctionFactory's 356,800 µA free balance, and RaffleFactory must ship with the new SDK (K6).

rolloutOrder.step: Fund PrizeBoxFactory with at least 0.1 ALGO and upgrade it
rolloutOrder.why: The factory has 0 balance, so the first mint reverts.

rolloutOrder.step: Deploy the Welcome plugin
rolloutOrder.why: It pins the factory and calls newAccount with automaticUpdates, which exists only after the factory upgrade.

rolloutOrder.step: Set guild_fees, then deploy GuildFactory and upload consensus programs in one guarded run
